newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Senate panel backs Holder for Justice post.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Senate panel backs Holder for Justice post.

text.p: The Senate Judiciary Committee Tuesday unanimously voted to confirm Eric Holder for the second-ranking position at the U.S. Department of Justice.
The full Senate must now confirm the nomination.

Holder, 46, has won bipartisan praise for his career as a federal prosecutor. He has supervised cases against international terrorists, drug kingpins, corrupt public officials and an attempted presidential assassin.

Holder, who would be the first black to occupy the number two post in the Justice Department, has also long been involved in community organisations, including a mentoring group called Concerned Black Men.

"He brings a wealth of valuable experience to the position, a position that plays a critical role in the day-to-day oversight, management and administration of the Department of Justice," said Judiciary Committee chairman Sen. Orrin Hatch, a Utah Republican.

President Clinton nominated Holder in March to fill one of several top jobs at Justice that have been empty for months. Clinton has recently announced his choices for other top jobs in the department.

Holder is the U.S. attorney for Washington, the city's top prosecutor for federal crimes. He has also worked in the Justice Department's elite Public Integrity Section, handling public corruption cases, and in 1988 President Ronald Reagan named him a judge on D.C. Superior Court, which handles local cases.
